pos.personaBrief: Telê's teams wanted the ball: the 1982 side kept it '60% do jogo' (Menotti via Telê 1992) and São Paulo was a 4-2-2-2 'com alta posse de bola' (pt.wikipedia); even against Newell's deep block they kept it on the ground and created chances. Counters appear (Atlético 1971, Palmeiras 1979) but as a by-product, not as giving up the ball.

pro.personaBrief: He rejected long balls and 'chutar a bola para qualquer lado' (1992), wanted the ball on the ground, but also called sterile backward circulation 'inútil' and 'um espetáculo feio' (1994) and did not want midfielders who only stop play (Falcão).

est.personaBrief: Falcão says he wanted them to play 'intuitively and not systematically'; 1982 midfielders rotated into the right-wing space, São Paulo swapped positions constantly (Cafu/Müller, 'linha de frente móvel', 'falta de referência') and his ideal was Holland 74 where 'todos jogavam em qualquer posição'.

lar.personaBrief: His best players were central (Zico, Sócrates, Falcão; Raí) and in 1982 he dropped a right winger to fit them; width came mainly from attacking full-backs (Leandro, Júnior, Cafu, Vitor, Ronaldo Luiz), and against a packed Newell's he said high balls would not score.

blo.personaBrief: He demanded that stars fight to win the ball back 'como um europeu' like Cruyff (1992) and the 1982 side closed down whoever was nearest; he sat deeper only as an exception v Bragantino in 1991, and his chances came from built-up play rather than high recoveries.

mar.personaBrief: No source states zonal or man-marking; the ball-oriented cover in 1982 ('whoever was closer to the ball had to close down') and his focus on his own team over the opponent point to space-based defending without dedicated markers.

pla.personaBrief: He preferred strengthening his own team to designing schemes against opponents (Trivela 2011), went for the win v Italy and said 'o time adversário se dane... nós vamos atacar' (1991), with pragmatic exceptions v Bragantino 1991 and in 1993.

res.personaBrief: He rejected the beautiful-vs-winning dilemma as 'balela' but said winning with a handball at 47 minutes 'não me satisfaz', that 'quem gosta de futebol gosta de ver aquele futebol de 82', and that good play is the coach's obligation with results as consequence (1992, 1994).

sis.personaBrief: In 1982 he gave stars freedom 'to try what we wanted' and played talent even at tactical cost, believing technique comes before tactics; by 1992 he demanded stars like Raí win the ball back, saying the waiting craque 'não existe mais'.

jog.personaBrief: 'Primeiro é o técnico' (1992): he drilled fundamentals daily, wanted midfielders who play rather than only stop, and rejected high balls; yet he praised Cafu's physical condition and in 1992 said a star who does not fight for the ball can no longer play.

bas.personaBrief: At São Paulo he bet on youngsters not yet trusted (Cafu, Leonardo, Antônio Carlos, Elivelton) who won titles, and 'revelou e elevou' many players; but Grêmio 1977 was 'só de jogadores experientes' and Raí and other established players were his core.

lid.personaBrief: 'Eu não admito indisciplina... seja jogador de nome ou que não tenha nome' (1991) and he cut Renato Gaúcho for arriving late in 1986; yet he consulted senior players on the 1991 final line-up and kept a more open, dialogue-based climate at Atlético 1971.
